name: Founding of Cambridge University
summary: After a violent dispute between Oxford scholars and townspeople in 1209, a group of masters and students migrated northeast to Cambridge, establishing a new school. The University of Cambridge grew slowly but steadily; Peterhouse, its first college, was founded in 1284. Over centuries Cambridge became Oxford's rival as the intellectual heart of England, producing Newton, Bacon, Milton, and Darwin among its alumni.
outcomes: Oxford scholars flee to Cambridge after town-gown riot
Rival to Oxford for seven centuries

_quarry.structural_significance: Cambridge University became one of the twin pillars of English higher education; its collegiate residential model shaped elite education worldwide.

sources_used: Leader, A History of the University of Cambridge Vol. I
